findings.reason: §37 must extend `_ENTRY_NAMES` or be descoped as §4 was, and its 5,297-stat premise has to be re-measured before it can name a remaining defect.
findings.text: §37 ("Resolving a resource lists its directory once per directory change") asks for exactly the mechanism that already shipped: `_ENTRY_NAMES` holds a directory's entry names against `metadata_index._dir_identity`, `_identity_listing` (`reckon/resources.py:819`) globs only when that identity moves, and `tests/test_plan_resolution_reads_the_directory_once_per_change.py` already asserts §37's three done-when cases (two passes over 200 plans cost one glob, an add+rename costs exactly one more, a rewritten sibling claiming a resolved slug is refused with `ResourceCollision`) — so a node dispatched on §37 would either write a second memo over the same glob or rewrite that committed test.

findings.reason: the section has to name which call it counts and either drop the stat ambition or justify a listing key that still moves on an in-place write.
findings.text: §37's stated cost is 5,297 `stat` calls in the identity index, but the held memo deliberately keeps stamping every sibling on each resolve (`reckon/resources.py:836–856`, and the docstring at `:807`) because a held stamp survives an in-place sibling rewrite that changes no directory entry; §37's deliverable ("lists that directory once") therefore either measures globs (already fixed) or asks to hold stamps, which would lose the refusal `tests/test_plan_resolution_reads_the_directory_once_per_change.py::test_a_sibling_rewritten_in_place_is_seen` protects.

findings.reason: §36 should say the per-entry reader is `current_discovery` and either add `reckon/_store.py` to its write paths or state why that second site keeps paying the whole-store validation.
findings.text: §36 ("A section ref resolves its target plan without building the project index") proposes a per-target resolution but `metadata_index.persisted_discovery_entries` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:1627`) plus `current_discovery` (`:1640`) already read the store once and validate one entry on demand, and `reckon/crew/admission/readiness.py:282–285` already uses that pair for exactly this purpose; the census of the same whole-index read on a few-plan need is `reckon/mcp.py:1976` (`_indexed_plan_states`, the site §36 targets) and `reckon/_store.py:909`, which calls `discovery_state(..., build=False)` and then `.get(relative)` — the hottest instance, running on every plan read's §3 seed — and `_store.py` is outside §36's declared write paths.

findings.reason: the brief should say the write parses the written bytes once and seeds `reuse_parsed_state`, so the change is a seed at one point rather than a new cache.
findings.text: §38 ("A plan write parses the written document once") proposes a single parse of the written document but does not name the mechanism that already makes that possible: `_plan_html.reuse_parsed_state` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1803`), added by §3, records a known parse under the file's own stat identity so every later reader (`read_state_file` → `read_state_and_text_file`, `reckon/_plan_html.py:1756`, `:1784`) takes it; the write's five parses are direct `read_state(text)` calls on raw strings (`reckon/_store.py:2194`, `:2197`, `:2324`, `:2442`), which bypass that seed.

findings.reason: the done-when's instrument and the deliverable's shape both need to name all the parsers, and a signature change on `section_coverage_gaps` would need `serve.py` and `doccheck.py` in the write paths.
findings.text: §38's done-when counts "the written document … through a patch on the document parser", but the write reaches the document through three entry points — `_plan_html.read_state` (`reckon/_store.py:2194`, `:2197`, `:2324`, `:2442`), `_plan_html.plan_headings` (`:2400`, `:2423` — five calls in the file), and `section_coverage_gaps`/`new_section_coverage_gaps` (`:2294`, `:2333`, `:2363`, `:2420`), the latter called also from `reckon/serve.py:3981` and `reckon/doccheck.py:1579` outside §38's write paths; a counter on `read_state` alone can read 1 while the write still builds five soups, so the design must hide the parse behind one private write-scoped helper that returns state, headings and coverage together, keeping the public helpers' signatures intact.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §38's design as written spreads a per-parse parameter across the write's call sites (`reckon/_store.py:2194`, `:2197`, `:2324`, `:2442`, `:2420`, `:2423`), instead of one private write helper that holds the parsed document and hands it to the version check, the heading guard and the coverage check.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §37 duplicates `resources._ENTRY_NAMES` with `_identity_listing` (`reckon/resources.py:816`, `:819`) is the owning mechanism, already covered by `tests/test_plan_resolution_reads_the_directory_once_per_change.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 3154, cli_options 535, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; none of §35 to §38 adds a public definition, a CLI option, an MCP view or a refusal family, so no section owes a retirement or merge (the counters they add are test-local patches).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §36 and §38 each propose a mechanism their codebase already owns: `metadata_index.persisted_discovery_entries`/`current_discovery` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:1627`, `:1640`) already resolve one entry without a project build, and `_plan_html.reuse_parsed_state` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1803`) already lets a writer seed the one parse a write must make.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §37 proposes a listing memo beside the one that exists (`reckon/resources.py:816` `_ENTRY_NAMES`, landed 2026-11-19) and does not say why that memo cannot be extended, nor that its stated stat cost is the per-sibling stamping that memo deliberately keeps.
